PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 34 years
Indication for Testing: Prenatal testing with ultrasound findings
Sample Type: Chorionic villus sample (CVS)
Gestational Age: [redacted]

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
Methodology: QF-PCR analysis performed on uncultured chorionic villi using fluorescently labeled STR markers

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 18 - ABNORMAL
Marker		Allele 1	Allele 2	Allele 3	Ratio	Interpretation
D18S976		142		146		150		1:1:1	Trisomy
D18S1002	156		160		164		1:1:1	Trisomy
D18S847		178		182		-		2:1		Trisomy
D18S978		204		208		212		1:1:1	Trisomy
D18S386		224		228		-		2:1		Trisomy
D18S390		186		190		194		1:1:1	Trisomy

CHROMOSOME 13 - NORMAL
All markers show normal biallelic patterns

CHROMOSOME 21 - NORMAL
All markers show normal biallelic patterns

SEX CHROMOSOMES - XY (MALE)
AMELOGENIN: X and Y peaks present
SRY: Positive

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy for chromosome 18 across six informative markers, consistent with Edwards syndrome. The pattern observed does not confirm meiotic origin of the non-disjunction. Chromosomes 13 and 21 show normal disomic patterns. Sex chromosome complement is consistent with male fetus (XY).

The ultrasound findings are consistent with these genetic results.

LIMITATIONS
- QF-PCR cannot exclude the possibility of a normal cell line (mosaicism)
- This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Analysis is limited to chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X and Y
- Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. G-banded karyotype analysis of cultured chorionic villi to follow for confirmation and to exclude mosaicism
2. Genetic counseling is strongly recommended to discuss:
   - Implications of trisomy 18 diagnosis
   - Correlation with ultrasound findings
   - Pregnancy management options
   - Recurrence risks for future pregnancies

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
[redacted date]
